chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ismail al-Bajali, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
If weeping does not come to you, then induce it; if a tear drops from you like the head of a fly, then give good tidings, give good tidings!

key_terms.الْبُكَاءُ: Weeping or crying, specifically in the context of religious devotion and humility before God.
key_terms.رَأْسُ الذُّبَابِ: The head of a fly; a common Arabic idiom used here to denote a very small quantity or size, referring to a single small tear drop.
key_terms.فَتَبَاكَ: Then weep/induce weeping; an imperative to actively produce tears if they do not come naturally.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of weeping in Shia spirituality and what counts as sufficient weeping?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the virtue of khushu' (humility) by instructing believers to induce tears even if they do not come naturally, highlighting that the physical manifestation of sorrow for sins is a gateway to spiritual purification. The comparison to the 'head of a fly' underscores that even the smallest sincere tear is highly valued in Shia tradition as a sign of a soft heart and divine mercy. This practice is rooted in the understanding that weeping is not merely an emotional release but a tangible act of worship that softens the heart against hardness and heedlessness.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah Bin al Mugheira, from Ismail Al Bajaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It the weeping does not come to you, and if there comes out from you (a tear drop) like the head of the fly, so congratulations, congratulations!’
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Isma’Il al-Bajilli from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
If weeping does not come through, make a weeping-like face. If of the size of the head of a fly tears come out that is your sheer good luck indeed.”
